items.name: Readability
items.evidence: The new helper `punycode(domain)` has a clear name and a docstring. It replaces inline `encode('idna').decode('ascii')` calls, and the existing `# IDN -> ACE` comments are kept. Formatting matches the surrounding code.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: One helper in django/utils/encoding.py replaces the copy-pasted idna conversion in message.py, validators.py and html.py. The conversion happens at the source in CachedDnsName.get_fqdn. There is no dead code or debug output.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: The existing `except UnicodeError` handlers in validators and html are kept. Nothing is swallowed in the mail path. Like the reference, `punycode(socket.getfqdn())` could raise on a malformed hostname, which is acceptable and does not fail silently.

items.name: Conversion is encoding-independent and safe for ASCII names
items.name_zh: 转换与编码无关且不影响 ASCII 主机名
items.evidence: `self._fqdn = punycode(socket.getfqdn())` converts the domain once at the source, so it works for every email.encoding. IDNA encoding leaves ASCII hosts unchanged, there is no try/except hiding failures, and the agent checked the output `@xn--p8s937b`.
